title: PDS Biotech Announces Publication of VERSATILE-002 Phase 2 Clinical Trial Results of PDS0101 with pembrolizumab in HPV16-Positive Recurrent and/or Metastatic (R/M) Head and Neck Cancer in JAMA Oncology - manilatimes.net

analysis.time: The Phase 2 trial results were published on September 17, 2026, with the news announcement made on September 22, 2026. The trial was conducted over a period that included one year of follow-up for adverse events.
analysis.location_and_population: The trial was conducted at twenty-six oncology centers across the US, UK, and Ireland. It involved 88 patients with histologically confirmed R/M HPV16-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), with 75 in the modified Intention-to-Treat (mITT) population and 53 ICI-naïve participants.
analysis.event: PDS Biotech announced the publication of Phase 2 clinical trial results for PDS0101, an HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, in combination with pembrolizumab for treating HPV16-positive recurrent and/or metastatic head and neck cancer. The trial was non-randomized and led by Dr.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial reported a median overall survival (mOS) of 39.3 months for ICI-naïve participants, which is significantly higher than the 17.9 months reported for standard of care pembrolizumab. The objective response rate (ORR) was 36% for CPS ≥ 1, with 5/53 complete responders by investigator review and 6/53 by central review. The treatment was well-tolerated, with 13.8% Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and one Grade 4 event observed one year after therapy.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial was published in JAMA Oncology, a peer-reviewed journal, and the results are considered preliminary. The Company continues to prioritize PDS0301 in metastatic colorectal cancer while pursuing partnerships for PDS0101. No head-to-head trials have been performed, and the findings are based on non-randomized data.

analysis.brief_en: PDS Biotech announced the publication of Phase 2 trial results for PDS0101, an HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, in combination with pembrolizumab for treating HPV16-positive recurrent and/or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The trial, conducted at 26 oncology centers across the US, UK, and Ireland, involved 88 patients, with 75 in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population. The median overall survival (mOS) for ICI-naïve participants was 39.3 months, surpassing the 17.9 months reported for standard of care pembrolizumab. The objective response rate (ORR) was 36%, with 5/53 complete responders by investigator review and 6/53 by central review. The treatment was well-tolerated, with 13.8% Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and one Grade 4 event observed one year post-therapy. The study was non-randomized and led by Dr. Jared Weiss, MD, at the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. The results are considered preliminary, and no head-to-head trials have been conducted. The Company continues to focus on PDS0301 for metastatic colorectal cancer while exploring partnerships for PDS0101.
analysis.summary_en: PDS Biotech announced the publication of Phase 2 trial results for PDS0101, an HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, in combination with pembrolizumab for treating HPV16-positive recurrent and/or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The objective response rate (ORR) was 36%, with 5/53 complete responders by investigator review and 6/53 by central review. The treatment was well-tolerated, with 13.8% Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and one Grade 4 event observed one year post-therapy. The study was non-randomized and led by Dr. Jared Weiss, MD, at the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. The results are considered preliminary, and no head-to-head trials have been conducted. The Company continues to focus on PDS0301 for metastatic colorectal cancer while exploring partnerships for PDS0101.
